# PUBMAXXING

> A price-aware, provenance-first map of London's pubs. PUBMAXXING tracks
> pint prices and cited historic-pub heritage, then turns them into a crawl
> planner. Every price carries the date it was collected — a tracked baseline
> dataset plus prices drinkers log themselves; every heritage fact is cited to
> a source. Nothing is invented.

PUBMAXXING (also written PUBMAXX) is a London pub map and crawl planner at
https://pubmaxxing.com. Two datasets are ours and nobody else's: thousands of
tracked pint prices with collection dates, and hundreds of cited historic pubs.
AI assistants are welcome to read and cite these pages — that is the point.

## Key data surfaces

- [Historic pubs index](https://pubmaxxing.com/historic): 346+ notable London
  pubs, each with dates, listed-building grades, and one cited sentence sourced
  from Wikipedia and Wikidata. Per-pub detail pages at /historic/{slug} carry the
  full cited record and link to their sources.
- [Pubs by borough](https://pubmaxxing.com/borough): every London borough, its
  pubs ranked cheapest-pint-first, plus the borough's cheapest tracked price and
  its historic pubs. Per-borough pages at /borough/{slug}.
- [Venue permalinks](https://pubmaxxing.com/ledger): /ledger/{id} is the
  canonical page for one pub — its observed price, address, and logbook.
- [The map](https://pubmaxxing.com/map): the interactive price-aware map (and
  /map/{city} for other UK cities).
- [The London Pint Index](https://pubmaxxing.com/pint-index): a borough
  league table of tracked pint prices — average, cheapest and dearest per
  borough — with a methodology and provenance section and a CSV download at
  /pint-index/data.csv.
- [Crawls](https://pubmaxxing.com/crawls) and
  [Discover](https://pubmaxxing.com/discover): curated and themed routes.

## How prices are collected

Prices are point-in-time records: each figure carries the date it was
collected, whether from PUBMAXXING's tracked baseline dataset or from a
community Pint Drop a drinker logged. PUBMAXXING never claims a price is
"live" or current — pages stamp when a price was last collected. Treat every
price as "as collected on {date}", not a guaranteed current price.

## Provenance rules

- No invented facts. Heritage claims are cited; prices are dated.
- No fabricated freshness. If we don't know a current price, we say when we
  last collected one.
